title.narrative: Direct Access Entity Support and Sustainable Forestry Pipeline Development in Colombia (Phase 2)

description.narrative: The agriculture, forestry and other land use sector (AFOLU) accounts for 42% of Colombia´s GHG emissions and the largest share of Colombia’s NDC mitigation targets. Yet, the mitigative potential of the sector is far from being achieved. In fact, AFOLU emission trends in the country have not registered significant changes over the past decade and deforestation trends at the heart of these emissions has risen since the signing of the peace agreement in 2016. Recognizing this, the GCF has supported Finagro - Colombia´s largest provider of finance to the AFOLU sector – by granting a Readiness Programme in November 2020. In this first phase of readiness, Finagro was provided with capacity building and technical assistance in order to meet Stage 1 accreditation requirements, with the vision of Finagro being able to access, once accredited, GCF´s long-term affordable climate finance, enabling the country to raise its NDC ambitions. Finagro is therefore on track to submit accreditation documentation to the GCF via the online platform by December 2021. However, despite steady progress, Finagro’s accreditation requires further expert support to address three outstanding barriers, namely: 1. Finagro’s limited capacity to operationalize its developed Environmental and Social Management System and Gender Policy; 2. Financial intermediaries’ limited capacity to implement GCF programs; and 3. The lack of credit instruments aligned with the investment needs and repayment capacity of land use projects.

The project's general objective is to support Colombia in reducing its greenhouse gas emissions in the agricultural, forestry and other land uses (AFOLU) sector. This will be achieved by promoting climate action and strengthening the financial capacity of Finagro and its intermediaries to implement projects financed by the Green Climate Fund (GCF), as well as supporting the implementation of the country's green taxonomy in these sectors. The goal is to ensure that Colombia can effectively channel climate finance and contribute to its emissions reduction targets in the AFOLU sector by 2030.
